subject: Pen test report: request for curated share & viewer option
messages:
From: Jordan Harper <security@evergreen-analytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request to review latest pentest and exec summary (NDA in place)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the SOC 2 artifacts last month. Our InfoSec team is now running a parallel review and requested the most recent penetration test report and an executive summary. We have the NDA executed (attached).

Two asks from my side:
- Can Redwood provide the pen test report with a short redaction matrix (indicating what will be removed or blurred) rather than a fully redacted bundle?
- If there is an internal policy that prevents sending PDFs, would Redwood consider a limited viewer (watermarked, time-bound) for the full report, plus a downloadable sanitized exec summary?

Timeline: our security review starts 11/17; would you be able to accommodate a delivery this side of that date?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Jordan Harper
Senior Security Program Manager
Evergreen Analytics

Attachment: evergreen_executed_NDA.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request to review latest pentest and exec summary (NDA in place)

Karthik / Alex — forwarding Evergreen's request. They have an NDA in place (attached). They want: a redaction matrix and either a sanitized exec summary + viewer for the full report OR a partially redacted PDF.

Constraints I know of: Legal prefers minimal permanent copies out the door; Security prefers a one-way viewer + redacted downloadable exec summary. We should confirm what level of redaction Legal needs (privileged findings? internal IP?), and whether PenTest Labs can produce a redaction matrix we can adopt.

Can you:
- Karthik: propose redaction boundaries (sensitive host identifiers, weaponized PoCs, customer-unique creds) — quick bullet list is fine.
- Alex: check with PenTest Labs whether they can produce a redaction matrix and if they're able to host the one-way viewer session (they usually deliver a ZIP/PDF).
- Ben: I'll keep Evergreen updated on delivery timeline and suggest our recommended approach.

Thanks — aiming to respond to Jordan by EOD with a plan.

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evergreen_executed_NDA.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request to review latest pentest and exec summary (NDA in place)

Thanks Naomi. Short proposal below — open to feedback from Legal (Alex) and Sales (Ben):

Redaction boundaries (security recommendation):
- Remove or generalize any customer-unique hostnames/IPs and cloud account IDs.
- Omit full exploit PoCs that contain step-by-step injection payloads or malware samples. Replace with high-level reproduction steps.
- Strip any discovered credentials, SSH keys, or ephemeral token strings.
- Aggregate low-risk vuln details into a summarized table (count by severity & category) instead of per-host traces.

Delivery options (ranked):
1) One-way viewer session (watermarked with viewer session attrs) for the full raw report + downloadable sanitized exec summary (PDF). This keeps the full forensic detail behind a hosted viewer.
2) Redacted PDF package created by PenTest Labs with our second-pass sanitization (they redact, we validate).
3) Full report delivered to an audited S3 bucket with access limited to Evergreen's security reviewers and time-bound credentials. Legal historically dislikes this.

Timeline feasibility: PenTest Labs can produce a redaction matrix in 3 business days after we confirm boundaries (they provided these last cycle). If we accept option (1), we can:
- Day 0: confirm boundaries and the exec summary template
- Day 1-3: PT Labs prepares redaction matrix + exec summary draft
- Day 4: Redwood runs validation pass and seeds one-way viewer session

I'll prepare the attached starter matrix (PTL_full_report_redaction_matrix.xlsx) and a sanitized exec summary draft (exec_summary_sanitized_v1.pdf). Alex — can you confirm Legal's comfort with option (1) and whether we need an addendum to the NDA for viewer-only access?

Karthik
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Harper <security@evergreen-analytics.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request to review latest pentest and exec summary (NDA in place)

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and for forwarding the NDA. We reviewed on our side. Short answer: we can accommodate a one-way, watermark-enabled viewer for the full pen test report and provide a downloadable sanitized executive summary. A few operational notes: 

- We will use PenTest Labs' redaction matrix as the baseline; Redwood will perform an additional validation pass focused on internal IPs and infra diagrams.
- Viewer sessions will be time-bound (default 14 days) and restrict printing/downloading. Each session will display a watermark with reviewer email and timestamp.
- We typically require a signed addendum to the NDA that lists "limited viewer access" as an acceptable delivery method — I'm attaching a short addendum template. If Evergreen is OK with the addendum, we can proceed without producing a second fully redacted PDF (saves time).
- Deliverables and ETA: assuming we agree to boundaries today, PenTest Labs + Redwood validation should have the viewer seeded and the exec summary PDF ready by 11/16 (we can compress if Evergreen needs earlier).

Jordan — please confirm whether the addendum is acceptable and whether the default 14-day viewer window is enough. If you prefer a shorter window, we can accommodate 7 days. Also confirm the reviewer list so we can bake those emails into the viewer session logs.

Ben — once Evergreen confirms, I'll shepherd the addendum for signature and coordinate Docusign if needed.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_viewer_addendum_draft.docx
